title: Meeting Chick Webb in 1936 and learning his secrets
summary: Jones recalls the summer of 1936, the Roseland opening, and Webb sharing tuning secrets and encouraging him.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: and then when I came into New York with Basie's band I met him in 1936 - it was the summer of 1936 and I was playing with Victor-Pillars. I left St. Louis and went back to rejoin Basie's band and when I got there, there was no band and no job. I had no thought of coming to New York, but fortunately somehow - it was the second week of July, 1936. We were fortunate enough to come into New York and open the Roseland Ballroom on the 24th day of December, which was Christmas Eve. The sign says: "Christmas Party, Count Basie, Woody Herman, and Zane Arthur". That was the Roseland Ballroom. I was leaving Count Basie and Chick Webb came down with Bardu Ali and his valet.
Bardu Ali, he was a singer, what -

He was the conductor. He fronted the band... I was going to leave and he said, "Well, my boy, why don't you stay and stick it out?" I said, "Well, Basie's here, he can get anything he wants." We developed a friendship and the man gave me some secrets that I could never divulge because I wouldn't know who to impart them to, evento my own son. I have never known the discussions I had with him. When he found out about my musical background; and what people did not know, this man was very musical. In later years since his death I have had the pleasure of playing his records and asking some of the young great

drummers to try to emulate - I said, "Let me hear you play this." They'd say, "He did all this?" I said, "Yes. They did it with a pair of sticks that looked pencils." Now you have to have all these two-pound weight sticks, to bang, bang, bang. No, no, no, he played the drums and he played them in tune." Mr. Chick Webb had also hung out with a fellow - also he got things from Mr. Drums, Mr. Walter Johnson. He told me; and when he found out that I tuned my drums, then he began to talk to me. He gave me some secrets.

This man, you could get any records of Mr. Chick Webb and you'll find out the system of his band. Although he was confined to the Savoy Ballroom, Chick had a band also and people forget that he played the Park-Sheraton.
